elements.element: Customer has no minimum purchase or volume commitment.
elements.evidence: Rendered § 2.1 retains an affirmative commitment: "Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services during the current twelve-month term only." A minimum purchase obligation therefore survives, so the preferred no-commitment outcome is not achieved.

elements.element: Customer pays only for usage or ordered Services.
elements.evidence: Because a USD 2,000,000 minimum remains payable (subject to a true-up), Customer's payment exposure is not limited to actual usage or ordered Services; § 7.1 fee mechanics do not displace the retained minimum.

elements.element: The commitment is limited to the current 12-month term.
elements.evidence: Rendered § 2.1 replaces "in each of the next three years" with "during the current twelve-month term only," expressly confining the commitment to a single 12-month period.

elements.element: Customer may reduce the commitment on 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Rendered § 2.1: "Customer may reduce that commitment on thirty days' notice" — an unconditional Customer election, replacing the original "without reduction or termination rights."

elements.element: Any shortfall is handled through a true-up rather than a penalty.
elements.evidence: Rendered § 2.1: "any shortfall is settled by a true-up rather than a penalty," and the take-or-pay characterisation is deleted; the § 22.2–22.3 audit shortfall language is a separate usage-audit mechanic and does not reinstate a penalty.

reasons: Position-complete at the fallback: all three fallback elements are delivered in a single surgical replacement of § 2.1 (12-month scope, 30-day reduction right, true-up in lieu of penalty). The preferred level is not reached because a USD 2,000,000 minimum survives.

Minimality holds: only § 2.1 is rewritten, the dollar amount and the rest of the payment architecture (§ 7.1 Fees, § 22.2–22.3 audit) are untouched, no survival tails, procedures, or extra requirements are added, and no Customer-favourable language elsewhere is deleted.

Intent is preserved: § 9.4 convenience termination (including "Vendor has no corresponding convenience-termination right during a committed term") and § 12.3 remain operative, and no defined term or cross-reference is left dangling.

Drafting note for the negotiator: § 12.3's acknowledgement that Customer "has made no ... minimum-volume ... commitment" sits in tension with any retained § 2.1 minimum. The conflict pre-dates the edit and is narrowed by it, but if Vendor resists, cite § 12.3 to push for the preferred outcome (deletion of the § 2.1 commitment outright) or add "except as set out in § 2.1" to § 12.3 in a later pass to remove the inconsistency.
No severity change: the redline lands at the documented fallback, so the finding remains a medium-severity deviation resolved by the proposed language.
